title: Establishment of in vitro 3D spheroid cell cultivation from human gynecologic cancer tissues
protocol: Collect tumor tissue for cell cultivation and extract DNA or RNA as soon as possible after surgical resection.
Place tumor samples for cell cultivation on ice in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) and transport to the laboratory.
Wash samples for DNA or RNA extraction with PBS, cut into small pieces, place in cryopreserved tubes, quickly freeze in liquid nitrogen, and store at −80°C.
Warm a bioshaker to 37°C.
Wash tissue samples with PBS 2 to 3 times for a few seconds.
Mechanically cut tumor into small pieces (approximately ~0.5 cm in size).
Transfer all tumor pieces to a 50-mL tube.
Add 10 mL of tissue processing buffer, 500 μL collagenase/hyaluronidase, 100 μL penicillin/streptomycin, and 200 μL amphotericin B.
Wrap the tube to prevent bacterial contamination.
Shake the tube in the bioshaker at 37°C at 200 rpm for 60 to 120 min.
Check the sample conditions at 60, 90, and 120 min after starting shaking.
Stop dissociation when the sample solution appears turbid or tumor volume decreases to approximately one-third of initial volume.
Filter the sample through a 100-μm cell strainer.
Rinse the tube with tissue processing buffer and filter rinses through the same cell strainer.
Centrifuge at 267 × g for 10 min at 15°C–25°C and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in DMEM/F12 medium to a total of 1 mL.
Add 4 mL density gradient centrifugation buffer and vortex for a few seconds.
Gently overlay 2 mL DMEM/F12 medium on the solution.
Centrifuge at 267 × g for 10 min.
Check the white layer between upper and lower solutions in a new 15-mL tube containing 5 mL DMEM/F12 medium.
Transfer the upper solution and the white layer to a new 15 mL tube using a 1,000 μL pipette.
Centrifuge at 267 × g for 10 minutes.
Discard the supernatant.
Check the cells if many dead cells remain.
Repeat steps 10–18 if necessary due to presence of many dead cells.
Add 1 mL ACK lysing buffer into the cell pellet if red blood cells form pellets.
Pipette several times for 10 minutes after adding ACK lysing buffer.
Add 5 mL PBS and repeat step 18.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL spheroid culture medium.
Count viable cells with trypan blue staining under a light microscope.
Adjust cell concentration to 1 × 10^4–10^6 cells/mL in spheroid culture medium.
Seed cells into an adequately sized dish.
Incubate at 37°C in a 5% CO2 humidified incubator.
Add Y-27632 (final concentration of 20 μM) and insulin (10 μg/mL) to the cultivation medium for colon cancer spheroid cells if needed.
For ovarian cancer spheroid cells, add Y-27632 and insulin as specified.
Tilt the dish for 30 seconds every 2-3 days.
Remove one-third of the medium from the dish and replace it with an equal volume of fresh medium.
Use fresh medium containing Y-27632 and insulin for ovarian cancer cells.
Transfer all cells and medium to a 10-mL tube, centrifuge at 267 × g for 5 minutes (alternative method).
Remove one-third of the medium from the tube after centrifugation and replace it with an equal volume of fresh medium (alternative method).
Mechanically dissociate large sphere-like structures by gently pipetting up and down with a 1-mL pipette tip.
Maintain spheroid cells without enzymatic dissociation until stable cell growth is confirmed.
Observe the formation and expansion of spheroids for 1–3 months to confirm stable cell growth.
Dilute cells at a ratio of 1:2 to 1:3 during initial passages.
Verify established spheroid cell lines after multiple enzymatic dissociations.
Change medium every 2-3 days when cultivation is stable.
Passage the spheroid cells every 10–14 days with dilution rates from 1:2 to 1:5 based on cell condition.
Collect cells in a 15 mL tube for passage.
Centrifuge collected cells at 267 × g for 5 minutes.
Discard supernatant after centrifugation.
Add adequate dissociation reagent solution (approximately 1 ml per 1 × 10^5 to 1 × 10^6 cells).
Determine dissociation conditions for each spheroid cell type at the initial passage.
Use Accumax or Accutase and pipette cells up and down 10–20 times with a 200-μL tip.
Incubate cells at 37°C for 5–10 min.
Repeat dissociation procedure until cells are mostly dissociated.
Centrifuge cell aliquots over 200 μl at 267 × g for 5 minutes to remove non-viable cells after dissociation (optional).
Add 3–5 volumes of PBS, centrifuge at 267 × g for 10 min, and discard the supernatant.
Resuspend cells with new spheroid culture medium.
Seed resuspended cells in a new cultivation dish.
Suspend the pellet in STEM-CELL BANKER.
Dispense the cell suspension into cryopreservation vials.
Store the vials at −80°C freezer for 14–17 h, then transfer to liquid nitrogen.
Remove frozen vials from liquid nitrogen and thaw quickly in a 37°C water bath for 5 minutes.
Centrifuge at 267 × g for 10 minutes and gently remove the supernatant.
Gently suspend the cell pellets in 1 mL spheroid culture medium and plate into a new culture dish.
Collect cells in a 15-mL tube.
Centrifuge the cell collection at 267 × g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Suspend the cell pellet in 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) for 1 to 3 h.
Centrifuge the PFA-treated cells at 267 × g for 5 min.
Discard the supernatant after centrifuging the PFA-treated cells.
Embed the cell pellet into paraffin blocks according to the standard protocol for paraffin embedding of tissue samples.
